text: Setting project goals is important for success. One useful way is to use SMART goals. This means goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal might be "redesign the homepage within two months." It also helps to set milestones, which are key points during the project. Deliverables are the final products or results you give to the customer. Finally, stakeholder alignment matters. This means everyone involved, like managers and team members, agrees on the goals. When everyone understands the same goals, the project is more likely to succeed.
